data.name: Lotfi
data.gender_notes: Lotfi is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'l-t-f', meaning 'to be heavy or weighty'. In Islamic tradition, this name signifies being noble and exalted in character. The name Lotfi carries the meaning “Noble, Exalted” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Lotfi usually hope their child will grow to embody noble, exalted and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Lotfi belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Noble, Exalted.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lotfi total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_arabic.name: لُطفي

in_arabic.long_meaning: أصل اللُطفي: اللُطفُ، العَطاء، الرَحمةُ، الإِنصافُ. في القرآن الكريم: لا يُستَبدَلُ اللُطفُ بالطَغيانِ. اللُطفي في الإسلام: المُتَفَرِّدُ باللُطفِ، المُتَفَرِّدُ بالرَحمةِ، منسوب إلى اللُطفِ، يُشير إلى المَنุษยِينَ الذين يُظهِرُونَ اللُطفَ في أَنفسِهِمْ وَتَعلَمُ الأَنفسُ ما يَخفى عَلى الأَعينِ. في التاريخ الإسلامي: اللُطفي كَأَسَماءِ سيدنا لُطفي بن مَيْمنان، أحدَ الصُحابةِ.

in_english.name: Lotfi
in_english.meaning: Lotfi, meaning 'blessed with kindness, mercy, and compassion', a name that symbolizes the qualities of a good person, someone who shows kindness, compassion, and mercy to others, and is known for their generosity, charity, and good deeds.
in_english.long_meaning: The name Lotfi has its roots in the Arabic word 'lutf', which means kindness, mercy, and compassion. In the Quran, the concept of lutf is contrasted with taghyan, or oppression. In Islamic tradition, Lotfi is a name that is associated with individuals who embody the qualities of kindness, mercy, and compassion. In modern times, the name Lotfi is still used in many Muslim cultures to signify a person who is blessed with good qualities and values.

It is rooted in the Arabic language, and its meaning—to be heavy or weighty—connotes strength, gravity, and importance. In many Islamic cultures, names hold great significance, and a child is often given a name that reflects the parents' hopes and dreams for their offspring. As such, the name Lotfi might be given to a child as a sign of the parents' aspirations for them to grow up to be thoughtful, influential, and revered individuals in their communities.

Being lotfy or weighty implies having a noble character, bearing an ethical and moral foundation upon which one's actions are based. The name is therefore a reminder for the bearer to strive towards virtuousness and righteousness in life. Furthermore, it is a constant encouragement to carry oneself with dignity, respect, and grace. By embodying a lotfy character, the individual not only nurtures their own growth and development but also contributes positively to their community and society at large, thereby promoting peace, compassion, and understanding.
